transcript: This play takes place in an actual apartment. I had missed its previous two sold out runs, so when I saw it was coming back, I knew I had to jump on a ticket. Now, this version of the show is a little bit different than previous versions. The previous runs were held at an apartment in Greenpoint to an audience of only six people per show, with everyone being fed soup mid show. This new production in lower Manhattan expands the audience size to 30, with only five audience members getting soup. And that is determined by the tier of ticket that you buy. The highest tier is the one that includes soup. And of course, you know, I had to buy one of those tickets because to me, that felt like the full Slanted Floors experience. And I will tell you about the soup later, but I wanna walk through the entire experience from start to finish. So you check in at the nearby Astor Place Theater and just kinda hang out in the lobby until it's ready for everyone to go over at once. The apartment is literally next door, so it's very easy to get to. But do beware, you do have to go up a small set of stairs if that's something that's difficult for you. Once you get into the apartment, there's no photo or video allowed at all. But it is an actual real life New York apartment, so it is quite cramped with Seating basically around the perimeter and then a little couch area where the five people who get soup sit. The basic premise is that you are a fly on the wall in this apartment, in this day, in a life of this queer couple, one of whom works a 9 to 5 and the other is a freelance artist. The soup comes into play when the two characters have dinner. They also serve the five audience members, and we all have soup together. Although I should note that this play is site specific but not immersive, meaning we, the audience, do not actually exist in the world of the play. And so while there are clever ways in which the production is able to involve the audience, including the soup moment, for the most part, the actors are not really gonna acknowledge you. And more importantly, they're not looking for you to do any improv with them or converse in any way. You are quite literally there to just be a fly on the wall. And in that sense, the play is very voyeuristic. You feel like you are listening in on conversations you're not really supposed to be listening in on. So if you're nosy like me, you'll probably enjoy it. No seat is really gonna be able to see everything, even where I was sitting in the most premium seat. While that can be frustrating at times, it is very much intentional and does contribute to this fly On the wall feeling. but it is certainly a very unique experience with or without soup. But I definitely recommend getting the soup. I think it's 100% worth it. It's like this spiced puréed squash. It comes with a little breadstick for you to dip. I thoroughly enjoyed it and I did think that it added to the experience. But even without the soup, it is still, I think, a worthwhile experience and I am very glad that I finally got a chance to check it out.
classificationReason: Creator attended the site-specific off-Broadway production of Slanted Floors, walking through the full experience from check-in at Astor Place Theater to the soup-included ticket tier. First-hand attendance and opinionated description of the production are clear.
